title: A desk that answered at the default is sent to setup by a later search
body:
## Summary
On a first launch the default desk answers and is kept, but the run keeps source DEFAULT, so the waiting screen's minute search (which skips that desk) ends on the setup screen, which never retries.

## Description
`stick-app/src/main/kotlin/dev/studydesk/stick/StickActivity.kt:279` searches the LAN every 12th tick of the error or pairing screen; `DeskNet.scan` drops the desk being tried (`stick-app/src/main/kotlin/dev/studydesk/stick/DeskNet.kt:81`), so with one desk on the LAN it finds nothing, and `Plan.afterScan` (`stick-app/src/main/kotlin/dev/studydesk/stick/Desk.kt:183`) returns Setup for source DEFAULT. `StickActivity.kt:227` applies it: "No desk answered at 10.0.0.141:3000 or anywhere on this network" over a desk that answers, on a screen with no tick. After a restart the same kept desk is SAVED and goes to the error screen instead (the pair). The Step.Setup doc says setup is for "no desk was ever kept". Registry: health-checks/three-state-outcomes (a remediation needs a definitive failure). Fixed: `Plan.answered()` makes a default that answered SAVED, applied on Open and Unpaired.

## Flow
- fresh install, open the app: the default answers as a guest -> pairing screen (source DEFAULT)
- wait 60 s for the operator's adb line -> the 12th tick's search skips the desk, finds nothing
- afterScan(DEFAULT) -> Setup: a false 'no desk' line, and no more retries
- fix: Plan.answered(DEFAULT)=SAVED on Open/Unpaired, so the search's empty result renders the waiting screen again

## Expected impact
The operator on a first launch (the pairing screen waits for his adb line) and any stick whose desk restarts for over ~90 s stay on a working screen that retries. Could break: nothing found on the setup path for a stick that never reached a desk (DEFAULT is unchanged there).

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - a found desk is never sent to the non-retrying setup screen
Before: afterScan(answered(DEFAULT), [], ...) = Setup; 1 of 5 sources reaches setup after a desk answered
After: Down(real); 0 of 5 (DeskTest, gate exit 0, 24 tests)
Method: gate - DeskTest case red with answered() as identity (exit 1), green after the fix; the Activity wiring is one line per branch and needs the device check
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
stick-app/src/main/kotlin/dev/studydesk/stick/StickActivity.kt:279 if (recovery.tick() && source != Source.GIVEN && source != Source.PICKED) { scan(quiet = true) ...
stick-app/src/main/kotlin/dev/studydesk/stick/DeskNet.kt:81 .filter { it != tried && Address.keepable(it) }
stick-app/src/main/kotlin/dev/studydesk/stick/Desk.kt:183 return if (source == Source.DEFAULT) Step.Setup(...)
stick-app/src/main/kotlin/dev/studydesk/stick/StickActivity.kt:227 if (quiet && step is Step.Down) render() else apply(step)
gate: a1-red exit 1 (24 tests, 1 failed) -> a1-green exit 0

title: KeyBridgeTest checked page names against its own copy, not keys.ts
body:
## Summary
The key bridge test claimed every name is one keys.ts maps but compared against a hand copy, and left 3 of 12 mapped Android codes untested.

## Description
`stick-app/src/test/kotlin/dev/studydesk/stick/KeyBridgeTest.kt` held a literal map of 9 codes to names and never read `desk/src/tv/keys.ts` (KEYBOARD at `desk/src/tv/keys.ts:29`). NUMPAD_ENTER, MEDIA_PLAY and MEDIA_PAUSE were untested. A test that reads the implementation's own list is coverage theater (SKILL 4.7). Fixed: the suite reads KEYBOARD (comments stripped) and checks each Android code reaches the page as a name keys.ts maps to the same button, and that the mapped set equals the spec.

## Flow
- seed MEDIA_PAUSE -> 'Pause' in KeyBridge.kt
- old suite: green (exit 0)
- new suite: red (exit 1, 1 of 25 failed)
- remove the seed: green

## Expected impact
A renamed or dropped key in keys.ts, or a mistyped bridge name, now fails the stick gate instead of a remote button doing nothing on the TV. Could break: the test reads a desk file, so a keys.ts restructure of KEYBOARD needs the parser touched.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - the bridge's names are checked against the desk's keymap
Before: 0/12 names checked against keys.ts; 9/12 codes covered; seeded mutation undetected
After: 12/12 and 12/12; seeded mutation red
Method: gate - seeded control on both suites
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
old KeyBridgeTest.kt: val seen = mapOf(... 9 entries ...) // no file read
desk/src/tv/keys.ts:29 const KEYBOARD = new Map<string, Key>([...])
seed MEDIA_PAUSE->'Pause': old suite exit 0; new suite exit 1 (25 tests, 1 failed)

title: KeyBridge's Android key codes are not checked against android.view.KeyEvent
body:
## Summary
KeyBridge spells twelve Android key codes as its own ints while StickActivity compares against KeyEvent's constants; nothing tied the two.

## Description
`stick-app/src/main/kotlin/dev/studydesk/stick/KeyBridge.kt:13-24` declares DPAD_UP=19 ... NUMPAD_ENTER=160 so the table runs on the JVM; `StickActivity.kt` uses `KeyEvent.KEYCODE_BACK` and friends for the same keys (onBack, onPanelKey). A mistyped constant maps a button the remote never sends and every test, which goes through the constant, stays green. Fixed: the suite asserts each of the 12 against `KeyEvent.KEYCODE_*` (compile-time constants inlined from the android.jar stubs).

## Flow
- seed MENU = 83
- every prior test: green
- new test: red (exit 1, 26 tests, 1 failed)
- seed removed: green

## Expected impact
A wrong constant fails the gate instead of leaving a remote button dead on the page. Could break: nothing; test-only.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - one vocabulary, two spellings, now checked
Before: 0/12 KeyBridge codes checked against KeyEvent; seeded MENU=83 green
After: 12/12; seeded MENU=83 red
Method: gate - seeded control
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
stick-app/src/main/kotlin/dev/studydesk/stick/KeyBridge.kt:20 const val MENU = 82
stick-app/src/main/kotlin/dev/studydesk/stick/StickActivity.kt:389 if (e.keyCode == KeyEvent.KEYCODE_BACK) return onBack(e, k)
seed MENU=83: exit 1, 1 failed of 26

title: The error screen asks about the Wi-Fi twice and ends a question with a full stop
body:
## Summary
Three probe reasons are already a Wi-Fi question; the error screen appended '.' and then asked the Wi-Fi question again.

## Description
`StickActivity.kt` rendered `"${why}.\n\nIs the desk running on the computer, and is the stick on the same Wi-Fi?"`. DeskNet's reasons at `stick-app/src/main/kotlin/dev/studydesk/stick/DeskNet.kt:37`, `:42` and `:43` end in '?', so the screen read "...same Wi-Fi as the computer?." followed by a second Wi-Fi question; an IOException message ending in '.' read "..". Fixed: `Words.downBody` in Desk.kt (plain JVM): a reason that ends in its own question is the question, and a sentence gets one full stop.

## Flow
- stick Wi-Fi off -> probe 'the stick has no network: is its Wi-Fi on?'
- screen: 'The stick has no network: is its Wi-Fi on?.' then 'Is the desk running ..., and is the stick on the same Wi-Fi?'
- fix: the reason alone; plain reasons keep the question

## Expected impact
Whoever reads the error screen on the TV sees one clean question. Could break: nothing else reads the body; device capture owed.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - the error screen's wording is right for every probe reason
Before: 3/13 reasons rendered '?.' plus a second Wi-Fi question; 'it broke.' -> 'It broke..'
After: 0/13; 'It broke.'
Method: gate - DeskTest red on the extracted old wording (exit 1, 2 failed), green after
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
stick-app/src/main/kotlin/dev/studydesk/stick/DeskNet.kt:37 "no route to it: is the stick on the same Wi-Fi as the computer?"
stick-app/src/main/kotlin/dev/studydesk/stick/DeskNet.kt:42 "the stick has no network: is its Wi-Fi on?"
stick-app/src/main/kotlin/dev/studydesk/stick/DeskNet.kt:43 "no route to ${desk.host}: is the stick on the same Wi-Fi as the computer?"

title: The probe's contract with the desk had no verifier
body:
## Summary
The stick's 'this is a desk and I am its TV' rests on a guest door, two fields and a viewer union on the desk side, all spelled as literals with no test reading the desk.

## Description
`Probe.read` (`stick-app/src/main/kotlin/dev/studydesk/stick/Desk.kt:124-133`) needs `viewer` in tv|phone|guest and `phoneUrl`; `Desk.probeUrl` is `/api/session`. The desk sides are `desk/src/proxy.ts:15` (OPEN: a guest may GET /api/session), `desk/src/lib/session/pairing.ts:232` (LOBBY: fields every view carries) and `desk/src/lib/session/store.ts:394` (Session.viewer). A rename there drops every stick to its error screen with every gate green. Fixed: DeskContractTest reads the three files (comments stripped) and checks them against Probe.read and probeUrl.

## Flow
- seed: Probe's viewer set without 'phone' -> DeskTest green, contract suite red
- seed: probeUrl '/api/sessions' -> door test red
- seeds removed: green (31 tests)

## Expected impact
A desk-side rename of the session door or fields fails the stick gate. Could break: a restructure of LOBBY or OPEN needs the parser touched.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - the in-tree contract has a verifier
Before: 0/3 contract facts checked against the desk's source
After: 3/3; two seeded controls red
Method: gate - seeded controls
Result: better
Gate: none

title: The tick loop re-arms after onStop and can crash the process after onDestroy
body:
## Summary
onStop removes the tick, but a probe already in flight re-posts it; after onDestroy the next tick submits to a shut-down executor.

## Description
`StickActivity.kt:151` removes the tick on stop, but every probe callback ends in `schedule()` (`StickActivity.kt:275`, `:286`, via `apply`), and `probe()` posts its answer whatever the lifecycle (`StickActivity.kt:203`, gated only by `gen`). So a Home press while a probe is in flight (often on the error screen: a failing connect takes 2 s of each 5 s tick) leaves the loop probing in the background for good, and a recovery there loads /tv in a stopped activity. After Back-leave, `onDestroy` (`StickActivity.kt:152`) shuts the executor down without bumping `gen`; the in-flight answer re-arms the tick, and the next `io.execute` throws RejectedExecutionException on the main thread. Registry: native-shell-integration (creation-names-reaper: the loop and the executor have no reaper). Fix: a started flag that schedule() honours, gen++ and removeCallbacks in onStop/onDestroy, and busy cleared when an answer is dropped.

## Flow
- error screen, a probe in flight -> Home
- probe answers -> schedule() re-arms -> probes every 5 s while stopped
- or: Back-leave with a probe in flight -> onDestroy shuts io -> answer re-arms -> tick -> io.execute -> RejectedExecutionException

## Expected impact
The stick stops probing the desk from the background and leaves without a crash. Could break: the resume path (onStart must restart the loop after a dropped answer cleared busy).

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - the loop stops when the activity stops
Before: simulated: a probe in flight at onStop re-arms the tick (3 schedule() call sites reachable from a probe answer); after onDestroy the next tick hits a shut-down executor
After: predicted: no probe log lines after Home; no FATAL after leaving from the error screen
Method: simulation - three walked cases (Home on the error screen, Home on the page, Back-leave during a probe); no device in this session and no Robolectric in the module
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: device: desk stopped, stick on the error screen; press Home within 2 s of a 'probe' log line; `adb logcat -s StickKeys` must show no 'probe' line after Home for 30 s; then Back-leave during a probe and grep logcat for 'FATAL EXCEPTION' / RejectedExecutionException

title: The WebView is never paused or destroyed: page audio outlives Home
body:
## Summary
StickActivity never calls web.onPause()/pauseTimers() or web.destroy(), so the TV page (its YouTube lesson, and main's new looping landing music) keeps running after Home.

## Description
`StickActivity.kt:92-111` creates the WebView with autoplay (`settings.mediaPlaybackRequiresUserGesture = false`, `StickActivity.kt:96`); onStop/onDestroy (`:151`, `:152`) touch only the tick and the executor. Main's 78299aa3 adds a looping landing/break track (desk/src/tv/useDeskSound.ts, `el.loop = true`) with no visibilitychange pause, and the lesson plays a YouTube clip. The tv-app 'clip plays after Home' card is the same gap in the other shell (never re-proposed; this is the stick's site). Registry: native-shell-integration/native-owned-stream (a view-owned stream should be suspended while nobody watches). Fix: web.onPause()+pauseTimers() in onPause/onStop, onResume()+resumeTimers() back, web.destroy() in onDestroy; the desk side may also pause on visibilitychange.

## Flow
- landing with music on (or a lesson clip playing) -> Home -> another app
- audio keeps playing from dev.studydesk.stick
- fix: the WebView paused with the activity

## Expected impact
A family switching to another app on the TV no longer hears the desk behind it. Could break: the page's SSE link pauses too, and must reconnect on resume (the page already shows 'Lost the desk link. Reconnecting.').

## Evaluation
Claim: user - no desk audio after leaving the app
Before: simulated: no WebView pause or destroy call in the module (0 of 4 lifecycle hooks: onPause/onResume/pauseTimers/destroy)
After: predicted: no active audio track for the package 2 s after Home
Method: simulation - walked the lesson clip, the landing music and Back-leave; needs the stick
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
stick-app/src/main/kotlin/dev/studydesk/stick/StickActivity.kt:96 settings.mediaPlaybackRequiresUserGesture = false
stick-app/src/main/kotlin/dev/studydesk/stick/StickActivity.kt:151-152 onStop/onDestroy: no web.onPause/pauseTimers/destroy
grep -n "onPause\|pauseTimers\|destroy()" stick-app/src/main -> 0 hits
instrument: device: play the lesson clip or the landing music, press Home, then `adb shell dumpsys audio | grep -A3 'dev.studydesk.stick'` (active player state) before and after the fix

title: Every panel keeps the screen on: an error screen holds the TV awake all night
body:
## Summary
FLAG_KEEP_SCREEN_ON is set once in onCreate, so the error, pairing and setup screens block the TV's screensaver and sleep indefinitely.

## Description
`StickActivity.kt:89` adds FLAG_KEEP_SCREEN_ON for the whole activity. When the desk's computer is off overnight the stick sits on 'The desk is not answering', retrying every 5 s, with a static panel and the TV never sleeping (power, burn-in on OLED sets). The page needs it (a lesson clip, the break clock); a waiting panel does not. Fix: set the flag in apply() for Mode.WEB and SEARCHING, clear it for DOWN, UNPAIRED and SETUP.

## Flow
- computer off at night -> heartbeat misses -> error screen
- the TV never reaches its screensaver or sleep timer
- fix: the flag follows the mode

## Expected impact
A TV left on the error screen sleeps on its own timer; the page keeps the screen on as now. Could break: a desk that comes back while the TV slept loads the page under a dark screen (it is woken by the next remote press).

## Evaluation
Claim: other - the TV is not held awake by a waiting screen
Before: simulated: 1 window flag for 5 modes, set unconditionally
After: predicted: KEEP_SCREEN_ON absent from the window flags in DOWN/UNPAIRED/SETUP
Method: simulation - the flag's single site read; the window flags need the device
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: device: stop the desk, wait for the error screen, `adb shell dumpsys window windows | grep -i KEEP_SCREEN_ON` for the stick's window, before and after; then the screensaver timer reached

title: A held Select, Menu or Play repeats into the page as fresh presses
body:
## Summary
Every repeated ACTION_DOWN goes to the page as a new keydown with no repeat flag, so holding Select acts on the next screen too.

## Description
`StickActivity.kt:390` sends `toPage(k, null)` for every ACTION_DOWN, repeats included, and `KeyBridge.script` (`stick-app/src/main/kotlin/dev/studydesk/stick/KeyBridge.kt:60-67`) builds the event without `repeat`, so the page cannot tell. `desk/src/app/tv/page.tsx:136` acts on each one. Arrows should repeat (the walk relies on it for octets on the panel); Select, Menu and Play should act once per press, as the panels already do (Select acts on release, `StickActivity.kt:429`). Fix: drop repeats (repeatCount > 0) for Enter/ContextMenu/MediaPlayPause in dispatchKeyEvent, and pass `repeat:true` on arrow repeats.

## Flow
- landing, hold Select ~1 s
- Enter, Enter, Enter... reach the page: the app opens, then its first stop is selected
- fix: one Enter per press

## Expected impact
A child holding the OK button opens one thing, not a chain. Could break: nothing relies on a held Select today (keys.ts has no hold gesture).

## Evaluation
Claim: user - one Select press is one action
Before: simulated: N repeats of DPAD_CENTER -> N page Enters (0 filtered)
After: predicted: 1 'key Enter taken' log line per held press
Method: simulation - walked held Select, held Menu, held Right; needs the remote
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
stick-app/src/main/kotlin/dev/studydesk/stick/StickActivity.kt:390 if (e.action == KeyEvent.ACTION_DOWN) toPage(k, null)
stick-app/src/main/kotlin/dev/studydesk/stick/KeyBridge.kt:61 val init = "{key:'...',code:'',keyCode:..,which:..,bubbles:true,cancelable:true}" // no repeat
instrument: device: `adb shell input keyevent --longpress DPAD_CENTER` on the landing, count `key Enter taken` lines in `adb logcat -s StickKeys` (before >1, after 1); a KeyBridge unit test pins repeat:true in the script for arrows

title: Any app on the stick can repoint it through the exported url extra
body:
## Summary
The exported launcher activity takes EXTRA_URL from any caller, opens it, and keeps it once it answers like a desk.

## Description
`stick-app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml:21` exports StickActivity (it must, for the launcher), and `StickActivity.kt:147` / `:167` act on any intent's `url`. An app installed on the stick can point it at a host that answers /api/session like a desk; `keep()` then makes it the kept desk, and the learner's TV shows that host's page with the key bridge driving it. The only intended caller is the operator's `adb shell am start` (STICK-APK-WALK, step 3), whose referrer is com.android.shell. Fix: accept the url extra only when `referrer` is the shell (or the activity's own package), and log a refused one.

## Flow
- another app: startActivity(StickActivity, url=http://x:3000/tv)
- the stick probes x; x answers like a desk; it is kept
- fix: a url from any caller but adb's shell is refused and logged

## Expected impact
Only the operator's adb line can point or pair the stick. Could break: the operator's line if Fire OS reports another referrer; the device check settles it before merge.

## Evaluation
Claim: other - only the operator can repoint the stick
Before: 1 exported entry point, 0 caller checks
After: predicted: adb `am start` accepted, another package's intent refused
Method: simulation - the threat needs a second app on the stick; the referrer Fire OS reports for `am start` is unrecorded
Result: better
Gate: policy-tighten
evidence:
stick-app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml:21 android:exported="true"
stick-app/src/main/kotlin/dev/studydesk/stick/StickActivity.kt:147 if (intent.hasExtra(EXTRA_URL)) point(intent)
stick-app/src/main/kotlin/dev/studydesk/stick/StickActivity.kt:167 val given = intent?.getStringExtra(EXTRA_URL)?.trim()
instrument: device: log `referrer` for the operator's `adb shell am start ... --es url` (expect android-app://com.android.shell), then a pure `Pointing.accepts(referrer, ownPackage)` unit test and an intent from a scratch debug package refused

title: The heartbeat reads the whole TV session; one over 4 MB reads as not a desk
body:
## Summary
The probe reads up to 4 MB of the TV's full session to find `viewer`, which the TV view puts last; past the cap the probe fails and three in a row drop the page.

## Description
`stick-app/src/main/kotlin/dev/studydesk/stick/DeskNet.kt:56-62` buffers the body up to 4 MB, every heartbeat (BEAT_MS 10 s) and every scan probe. For the TV, `view()` returns `{ ...seen, viewer: "tv" }` (`desk/src/lib/session/pairing.ts:277`) and `viewer` is not a stored key (`desk/src/lib/session/store.ts:393-394`), so it is the LAST key: the probe needs the whole body, and when the session (history, memory, pages, essays) passes 4 MB `Probe.read` (`stick-app/src/main/kotlin/dev/studydesk/stick/Desk.kt:131-132`) returns 'something answered, but not a Study Desk'. That collapses 'unverifiable' into 'failed' (registry: health-checks/three-state-outcomes), and three of those take the page down. Fix: stream the body keeping its head and a rolling tail (64 KB each), and read the fields from those; the heap per beat falls with it.

## Flow
- a TV session grows past 4 MB
- heartbeat: the 4 MB head has no viewer -> Failed
- three beats -> the error screen over a running desk
- fix: head+tail read -> Answered(tv), at 128 KB per probe

## Expected impact
A large session no longer looks like a dead desk, and each heartbeat holds kilobytes, not megabytes, on a 1 GB stick. Could break: a body whose fields sit in the middle (not the desk's shape).

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - a large session is still recognised; performance - bounded heap per heartbeat
Before: body held per probe: up to 4 MB; a >4 MB TV session -> Failed
After: predicted: 128 KB; Answered(tv)
Method: simulation - the JVM reproduction (an HttpServer serving 5 MB with viewer last) and the real TV-view size are the instrument; this round built the contract test instead
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: JVM test with com.sun.net.httpserver.HttpServer serving a 5 MB JSON with viewer last (Failed before, Answered after) plus `JSON.stringify(view(s,'tv')).length` over the seeded test sessions to size the real body

title: The panels' lit stop is colour only, so VoiceView cannot say which is lit
body:
## Summary
The Retry / Change address chips and the address picker mark the lit one only by fill colour; nothing is selected, focused or announced.

## Description
`StickActivity.kt:368-379` (`chip`) sets text, colours and a stroke; the lit chip differs by `setColor(if (lit) AMBER else CHIP)` alone. No view takes focus, `isSelected` is never set, and the title of the error screen is not a live region, so Fire TV's VoiceView reads nothing when the stick drops to the error screen or the D-pad moves. Fix: `isSelected = lit` and a contentDescription with the stop's role ('Retry, 1 of 2, selected'), `accessibilityLiveRegion = POLITE` on the title, and an announcement when the lit stop changes.

## Flow
- VoiceView on, desk stopped -> error screen appears silently
- Right -> Change address lit; nothing is spoken
- fix: the title is announced; each move speaks the lit stop

## Expected impact
A learner or operator using VoiceView can use the error, pairing and setup screens. Could break: nothing visual.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - the panels are usable with VoiceView
Before: 0 of 3 accessibility properties on chips or title (selected, contentDescription, live region)
After: predicted: uiautomator dump shows selected=true on the lit chip
Method: simulation - needs the stick with VoiceView
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
stick-app/src/main/kotlin/dev/studydesk/stick/StickActivity.kt:372 setTextColor(if (lit) PANEL else INK)
grep -n "isSelected\|contentDescription\|accessibilityLiveRegion\|announceForAccessibility" stick-app/src/main -> 0 hits
instrument: device: `adb shell uiautomator dump` on the error screen before/after (selected attribute on the lit chip), then a VoiceView pass

title: Nothing in the log says which stick-app build is running
body:
## Summary
Walks and perf passes read the stick through logcat 'StickKeys', but no line names the APK build, so a capture cannot be tied to a build.

## Description
`stick-app/build.gradle.kts:20-21` pins versionCode 1 / versionName 0.1 for every build, and `StickActivity.onCreate` logs no identity. The APK walk had to explain that 'the check ran on the build just before two wording changes' (docs/concepts/STICK-APK-WALK-2026-10-20.md) and the perf passes say only 'the debug APK as installed'. Fix: one Log.i at onCreate with versionName and the package's lastUpdateTime (no build change), or a git sha through BuildConfig.

## Flow
- install a new build, run a walk
- logcat: keys, probes, steps, no build identity
- fix: 'stick-app 0.1 installed 2026-10-21T17:04' first in the log

## Expected impact
Every walk log carries its build. Could break: nothing.

## Evaluation
Claim: other - a log ties to its build
Before: 0 identity lines per launch; versionCode 1 for every build
After: predicted: 1 per launch
Method: simulation - logcat needs the stick
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
stick-app/build.gradle.kts:20 versionCode = 1
stick-app/build.gradle.kts:21 versionName = "0.1"
stick-app/src/main/kotlin/dev/studydesk/stick/StickActivity.kt:186 the first log line of a run is 'trying <desk>'
instrument: device: `adb logcat -s StickKeys` after a launch shows the identity line; compare two installs

title: No CI job, gate table or manifest capability runs the stick-app tests
body:
## Summary
quality.yml runs only :core:test; AGENTS.md's commands and gate tables, the manifest capabilities and the scan-sweep overlay never name :stick-app:testDebugUnitTest.

## Description
The module is in `settings.gradle.kts:19` and has 31 JVM tests after this round, but `.github/workflows/quality.yml:43` runs `node tools/gradlew.cjs :core:test` only, and a grep for 'stick' over `.github/workflows/`, `AGENTS.md`, `.ai/manifest.yaml` and `.claude/scan-sweep/config.md` finds nothing. A stick change is gated by whoever remembers the task name. Fix (repo-governance's paths): add `:stick-app:testDebugUnitTest` to quality.yml (the runner has the Android SDK), a row to both AGENTS.md tables and the overlay's Gates.

## Flow
- a PR edits stick-app or desk/src/tv/keys.ts
- CI runs no stick test (the keys.ts contract test included)
- fix: quality.yml runs the stick suite

## Expected impact
The contract tests built this round (keys.ts, the session door) run on every PR that could break them. Could break: CI time (+~1 min configure for the Android plugin).

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - the stick suite is gated
Before: 0 of 4 governance surfaces name stick-app
After: predicted: 4 of 4; a PR renaming a keys.ts key goes red
Method: simulation - out of this round's paths (repo-governance owns them)
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
grep -rn stick .github/workflows AGENTS.md .ai/manifest.yaml .claude/scan-sweep/config.md -> 0 hits
.github/workflows/quality.yml:43 run: node tools/gradlew.cjs :core:test --console=plain
settings.gradle.kts:19 include(":stick-app")
instrument: a PR that seeds a keys.ts rename on a branch: the quality job must go red on KeyBridgeTest; gate exit codes before/after the workflow edit

title: The waiting screens' decision lives untested in the activity
body:
## Summary
onTick's five-branch decision for the error and pairing screens, and scan's handling of its step, sit in StickActivity where no test reaches; the setup bug fixed this round lived on that seam.

## Description
`StickActivity.kt:267-292` decides, per probe answer and mode, between Open, Unpaired, Down, re-render and a quiet search, reading `source`, `key` and `mode`; `StickActivity.kt:223-227` decides whether a search moves the desk and whether a quiet result re-renders. Plan/Recovery/Heartbeat in Desk.kt are tested; these branches are not (0 of 7).
